providerStates.name: HOBO-546 reference fixture package is available

quickstartFixtureRefs.marketplaceUse: browse cards use accepted manifest fixture ids instead of inventing resource lifecycle behavior
search result warnings reuse plan-preview proof-mode wording
installability copy can cite accepted deploy evidence without building install runtime
listing detail stale-evidence labels reuse the accepted manage fixture
scope-out recovery label prevents marketplace UI from implying live remediation

wireframes.title: Browse grid with visible listing state and proof-mode chips
questionsAnswered: Which listings are visible, preview-only, beta, installable, blocked, deprecated, or yanked before the user clicks?
What evidence and owner route explain why a card can or cannot expose install intent?

wireframes.title: Search results with org-catalog filter and blocked-state explanation
questionsAnswered: Which policy, trust, catalog, or evidence boundary removed or downgraded a search result?
Can a reviewer see why ratings or publisher identity did not make the listing installable?

wireframes.title: Listing detail with trust evidence, stale warning, deprecation, and owner route
questionsAnswered: Which evidence source, customer-safe message, and support handoff are visible on detail pages?
When a listing is deprecated or stale, what migration or support action replaces install intent?

wireframes.title: Installability outcome panel with customer-safe message and scope-out guard
questionsAnswered: Does the panel have enough provenance, conformance, security, catalog, and policy evidence to show installability?
What exact text is shown when install runtime, registry, policy, or support execution is out of scope?

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Preview listing is visible for evaluation but cannot be presented as installable.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: not in org catalog; workspace admins see an evaluation-only state
fixtures.trustEvidence: publisher identity present; security review and catalog approval incomplete
fixtures.supportHandoff: route questions to marketplace trust owner with launch-limit wording

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Limited-beta listing is available only to allowed scopes with explicit missing-evidence limits.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: approved for beta workspace scope with policy pin required
fixtures.trustEvidence: limited-beta approval recorded; conformance evidence still bounded
fixtures.supportHandoff: route blockers to capability review owner before expanding visibility

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Listing is installable only because provenance, conformance, security review, catalog, and policy evidence are present.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: approved in org catalog with immutable version pin and support owner
fixtures.trustEvidence: signed provenance, conformance certificate, security review, and org catalog approval exist
fixtures.supportHandoff: attach evidence links and approved scope before any customer action

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Listing is blocked for this workspace by catalog, policy, trust, or approval state.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: blocked for current workspace; no install intent is exposed
fixtures.trustEvidence: policy pin denies this scope even though listing metadata remains visible
fixtures.supportHandoff: show owner route and denial evidence without granting override

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Deprecated listing remains visible only for migration guidance and existing-use explanation.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: deprecated entry remains audit-visible with replacement route
fixtures.trustEvidence: deprecation notice and replacement evidence exist; new install is not default
fixtures.supportHandoff: route to migration owner and support-safe replacement guidance

fixtures.customerSafeMessage: Yanked listing is removed from new selection and routed to support or migration guidance.
fixtures.orgCatalogDisposition: retired from org catalog selection and retained for audit only
fixtures.trustEvidence: yank decision exists; production registry removal stays out of this proof
fixtures.supportHandoff: send redacted customer-safe yank reason to support owner

scenarioPaths.narrative: Browse and installability panel show one listing as installable only after all evidence sources exist.
scenarioPaths.accessibilityNote: Keyboard focus reaches state, evidence source, owner route, and proof-mode chip in order.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: show install intent copy while naming the evidence owner and fixture source

scenarioPaths.narrative: Policy-blocked and yanked listings keep state visible but suppress install intent.
scenarioPaths.accessibilityNote: Blocked and yanked states are text labels, not color-only badges.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: route to org catalog or support owner without granting override

scenarioPaths.narrative: Preview-only and limited-beta listings carry missing-evidence language rather than optimistic install claims.
scenarioPaths.accessibilityNote: Screen reader copy announces missing evidence and limited-beta status.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: show warning copy and review owner before selection

scenarioPaths.narrative: Deprecated and yanked listings expose customer-safe support or migration wording.
scenarioPaths.accessibilityNote: Responsive layout keeps support route and customer-safe message adjacent.
scenarioPaths.safeOutcome: handoff support-safe deprecation or yank evidence with no live ticket creation

accessibilityNotes: Keyboard order moves from browse/search result to listing detail and then installability panel actions.
Screen reader labels include visible state, evidence source, owner route, proof mode, and support handoff.
Contrast and text labels distinguish preview, beta, installable, blocked, deprecated, and yanked states without relying on color.
Responsive layouts keep customer-safe message, org-catalog disposition, and owner route visible on narrow screens.
Motion is optional; warning and status transitions must respect reduced-motion preferences.
scopeOut: No live storefront, browse/search service, marketplace service, or install runtime.
No Registry storage, resolver, package hosting, signing, or install-time verification implementation.
No ranking, recommendation, paid placement, monetization, payout, or commercial marketplace policy.
No publisher portal workflow, evidence upload service, maintainer workflow, or submission tooling.
No policy engine, RBAC runtime, scanner integration, conformance runner, or approval service implementation.
No support tooling, notification delivery, launch publication, or customer-facing launch claim without evidence.
